$comment: The VS Code extension's errorLens.replace rules (ark/extension/package.json) and how ErrorLens v3.30.0 applies them. cases.json holds inputs and expected outputs; errorLens.ts is a reference implementation.

semantics.order: Rules are tried in order on the whole message; the first whose matcher matches anywhere wins and no later rule runs.
semantics.substitution: The output starts as the rule's message. For each group N from 0 to the last, every `$N` in it is replaced, as JavaScript's String.prototype.replace(new RegExp('\\$N', 'gu'), groupN) does: replacement patterns in the group's text ($&, $$, $`, $') are expanded, and a group that didn't participate becomes the text 'undefined'.
semantics.noMatch: A message no rule matches is shown unchanged.
semantics.input: The diagnostic message as VS Code's TypeScript extension gives it: tsserver flattens a message chain with '\n', indenting each level two more spaces.
semantics.display: ErrorLens then draws the message after the line: with its defaults, each run of \n, \r and \t becomes ⏎ and a message over 500 code points is cut to 500 and ends with ….

rules.matcher: ^(?:Type|Argument of type) '"(.*)"' is not assignable to (?:parameter of )?type '("\1.*")'\.
